solution_steps.note: Enter the missing required probe (clears MISSING_PROBE).

Re-enter CEP8 with the technologist's ABNORMAL call. 12/200 = 6.0% is at/above the synthetic 2.5% cutoff, so a NORMAL call was an INTERP_CONSISTENCY ERROR. The row is upserted; the earlier value is not retained.
Validation now has no ERROR findings; the stored findings from the blocked run are replaced and the order finalizes.

question_answers.answer: MISSING_PROBE (ERROR): required probe TP53_17p has no result. INTERP_CONSISTENCY (ERROR): CEP8 is 12/200 = 6.0% abnormal, at or above its synthetic 2.5% cutoff, but called NORMAL. Both come from validation.validate_order; any ERROR finding blocks finalization.

Ingestion checks message structure, order matching, specimen, probe codes, integer counts, abnormal <= scored, and the interpretation vocabulary only. Required-probe completeness and cutoff consistency belong to validation.validate_order, which runs at finalization, so a partial or inconsistent but well-formed panel files.

One. fish_result is UNIQUE(order_id, probe_id) and workflow.enter_fish_result upserts, so the CEP8 row was updated in place (same result_id). The earlier counts and pattern are not retained; only the RESULT_ENTERED audit details remain, 'probe=CEP8 interp=NORMAL' then 'probe=CEP8 interp=ABNORMAL', and they record probe and interpretation only.

workflow.run_validation replaces an order's stored findings on every run (_persist_findings deletes, then inserts). The blocked run stored two ERROR rows; the successful run found none, so no validation_error rows remain.
VALIDATION_RUN 'findings=2 errors=2' followed by FINALIZE_BLOCKED '2 blocking error(s)'; later VALIDATION_RUN 'findings=0 errors=0', REPORT_FINALIZED, and FINALIZED.
